entries.test: Compare Shumer's factual claims about AI reliability with contemporaneous public evaluations and documented system performance.
entries.note: The loaded description includes a substantive allegation of factual errors. Marcus is quoting his own statement to a journalist.

entries.test: Inspect Shumer's post and its supporting references for data demonstrating error-free creation of whole complex apps by the latest coding systems.
entries.note: This concerns evidence Shumer supplied, rather than whether such systems can actually perform the task.

entries.test: Compare METR's published benchmark methodology with Shumer's account to establish its success threshold, task coverage, and whether he omitted those limitations.
entries.note: The normalization drops the allegation that Shumer omitted these limitations and adds a broader conclusion about what the benchmark demonstrates.

entries.test: Examine public evaluations of systems available at publication across human-performable five-hour tasks, alongside documented rates of hallucinations and everyday errors.
entries.note: The claim concerns systems available when the post was published.

entries.test: Compare the capabilities and reliability portrayed in Shumer's post with contemporaneous public demonstrations, evaluations, and documented failures.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion anchors 'isn’t realistic' to concrete claims about capabilities and reliability.

entries.test: Check public coding-speed demonstrations and the cited TechCrunch reporting for coders reporting burnout alongside relatively modest productivity gains.
entries.note: The burnout and gains claim is about what some coders report, not a measured effect across all coders.

entries.test: Compare public evaluations of recent and preceding coding systems on completing coding tasks successfully with fewer human interventions.
entries.note: The context supplies a plain reading: increased capacity to work autonomously, with success still intermittent.

entries.test: Examine contemporaneous public security audits and reporting for documented vulnerabilities and unresolved security concerns in AI-generated code.
entries.note: This asserts an existing security concern, without claiming that all generated code is insecure.

entries.test: Examine public trends in AI-generated code production together with contemporaneous security and correctness evaluations establishing whether its reliability remained unresolved.
entries.note: The uncertainty concerns the existing evidence for security and trustworthiness; it is not a probabilistic forecast.
The extracted proposition is a judgment about how readers should have treated the post.
